1: # Pathland Rust Workspace
2: 
3: The Rust core of Pathland: the **opcode engine** that emits the declarative
4: view structure as a fixed 16-byte opcode ring buffer into shared linear memory,
5: consumed by host renderers. Runs natively on desktop (C ABI + GTK renderer);
6: WASM/WIT is the browser/remote projection only.
7: 
8: ```
9: crates/
10: ├── pathland-opcode/   # 16-byte opcode, ring buffer, bump arena, linear-memory layout (no_std)
11: ├── pathland-view/     # SwiftUI-style view DSL: VStack/HStack/Text/Button + decoupled
12: │                      #   chainable modifiers (spacing/padding/fontSize/color/background) (no_std)
13: ├── pathland-engine/   # retained view tree -> declarative TREE/STYLE opcodes,
14: │                      #   diff-based reactive emission (zero-alloc steady state)
15: ├── pathland-host/     # host reader: ring -> native-element description (std layer)
16: ├── pathland-transport/# opcode transport: shared-memory ring + network batch encode/decode
17: │                      #   + batching policy + transport abstraction (RingTransport/FrameSource)
18: ├── pathland-guest/    # WASM guest component: retained tree + engine + emit/take-batch (browser)
19: ├── pathland-wit-host/ # WIT host bindings + DSL bridge (wasmtime embed, remote hosts)
20: ├── pathland-native/   # native C-ABI shim + NativeHost: flat world over a zero-copy shared ring
21: ├── pathland-gtk/      # GTK4 RENDERER (rlib + cdylib): opcode frames -> native GTK widgets
22: │                      #   (incremental); the only crate that touches GTK/glib/pango
23: ├── pathland-codegen/  # DSL code generator: parses lib/ui/components.yaml, asserts ids,
24: │                      #   emits the checked-in Java DSL
25: └── pathland-gtk-demo/ # GTK4 desktop demo: authors the DSL, renders through pathland-gtk
26:                        #   (uses NO GTK APIs directly)
27: 
28: # Cross-language demo
29: ../java/pathland-demo/ # Java (Maven): SwiftUI-like DSL + JNA over pathland-native,
30:                        #   rendered through pathland-gtk (uses NO Swing / NO GTK APIs)
31: ```
32: 
33: ## Specification
34: 
35: - [`spec/OPCODE.md`](../../spec/OPCODE.md) — the 16-byte opcode protocol
36: - [`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`](../../spec/CONFORMANCE.md) — golden byte vectors
37: - [`wit/pathland.wit`](../../wit/pathland.wit) — the WIT component world
38: 
39: ## Run tests
40: 
41: ```bash
42: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo test
43: ```
44: 
45: ## Run the GTK desktop demo (native, zero-copy shared ring)
46: 
47: ```bash
48: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo run -p pathland-gtk-demo
49: ```
50: 
51: Requires GTK4 (`brew install gtk4` on macOS).
52: 
53: ## Run the Java demo (cross-language, JNA over the native C-ABI shim + GTK renderer)
54: 
55: ```bash
56: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo build -p pathland-native -p pathland-gtk
57: cd ../java/pathland-demo && mvn -q -Dpathland.rust.target=<lib/rust/target/debug> compile exec:java
58: ```
59: 
60: On macOS, GTK must run on the main thread: prefix the mvn command with
61: `MAVEN_OPTS="-XstartOnFirstThread"`.
62: 
63: The Java app uses a SwiftUI-like DSL, drives the Rust engine via the flat
64: `pathland_native_*` C ABI (no per-component wrappers), and renders through the
65: shared `pathland-gtk` renderer (in-process via JNA). It uses **no Swing and no
66: GTK APIs directly** — native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes through the
67: shared ring, and the host drains them via `pathland_native_drain_events`. Verify
68: headlessly with `-Dexec.mainClass=demo.DemoHeadless`.
69: 
70: 
71: ## Build for wasm32 (browser projection only)
72: 
73: ```bash
74: RUSTC=~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/rustc \
75:   cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
76: ```
77: 
78: > The Homebrew `cargo` on PATH resolves a rustc without the wasm std. Use the
79: > rustup toolchain's rustc via `RUSTC=...` (or `rustup run stable cargo`).
80: 
81: ## Engine example
82: 
83: The engine emits declarative structure (no rects). A signal changes a property;
84: the next `emit` writes only the delta opcodes.
85: 
86: ```rust
87: use pathland_engine::Engine;
88: use pathland_opcode::{init_memory, Guest, MemoryLayout};
89: use pathland_view::{assign_ids, text, vstack, View, ViewExt};
90: 
91: let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
92: let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
93: init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
94: 
95: let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);
96: let mut engine = Engine::new();
97:

99:     .spacing(4.0)
100:     .padding(8.0)
101:     .build();
102: assign_ids(&mut root, &mut 1);
103: 
104: guest.begin_frame();
105: engine.emit(&root, &mut guest).unwrap(); // full structure
106: guest.end_frame();
107: 
108: root.properties.insert(pathland_opcode::property_id::SPACING, 12.0f32.to_bits());
109: 
110: guest.begin_frame();
111: engine.emit(&root, &mut guest).unwrap(); // exactly one SET_PROPERTY
112: guest.end_frame();
113: ```
114: 
115: Emission in the steady state allocates nothing; only changed nodes produce
116: opcodes, so an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes. Native renderers map the
117: structure onto their native elements (GTK4 widgets, DOM elements).
118:

122: on a time/size policy (`BatchEncoder` / `Batcher`); a `BatchDecoder` rebuilds a
123: `Frame`-compatible view so the same `RenderTree::apply_frame` consumes batches
124: and shared-memory frames identically. See `spec/OPCODE.md#transport`.

# Pathland Rust Workspace

The Rust core of Pathland: the **opcode engine** that emits the declarative
view structure as a fixed 16-byte opcode ring buffer into shared linear memory,
consumed by host renderers. Runs natively on desktop (C ABI + GTK renderer);
WASM/WIT is the browser/remote projection only.

```
crates/
├── pathland-opcode/   # 16-byte opcode, ring buffer, bump arena, linear-memory layout (no_std)
├── pathland-view/     # SwiftUI-style view DSL: VStack/HStack/Text/Button + decoupled
│                      #   chainable modifiers (spacing/padding/fontSize/color/background) (no_std)
├── pathland-engine/   # retained view tree -> declarative TREE/STYLE opcodes,
│                      #   diff-based reactive emission (zero-alloc steady state)
├── pathland-host/     # host reader: ring -> native-element description (std layer)
├── pathland-transport/# opcode transport: shared-memory ring + network batch encode/decode
│                      #   + batching policy + transport abstraction (RingTransport/FrameSource)
├── pathland-guest/    # WASM guest component: retained tree + engine + emit/take-batch (browser)
├── pathland-wit-host/ # WIT host bindings + DSL bridge (wasmtime embed, remote hosts)
├── pathland-native/   # native C-ABI shim + NativeHost: flat world over a zero-copy shared ring
├── pathland-gtk/      # GTK4 RENDERER (rlib + cdylib): opcode frames -> native GTK widgets
│                      #   (incremental); the only crate that touches GTK/glib/pango
├── pathland-codegen/  # DSL code generator: parses lib/ui/components.yaml, asserts ids,
│                      #   emits the checked-in Java DSL
└── pathland-gtk-demo/ # GTK4 desktop demo: authors the DSL, renders through pathland-gtk
                       #   (uses NO GTK APIs directly)

# Cross-language demo
../java/pathland-demo/ # Java (Maven): SwiftUI-like DSL + JNA over pathland-native,
                       #   rendered through pathland-gtk (uses NO Swing / NO GTK APIs)
```

## Specification

- [`spec/OPCODE.md`](../../spec/OPCODE.md) — the 16-byte opcode protocol
- [`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`](../../spec/CONFORMANCE.md) — golden byte vectors
- [`wit/pathland.wit`](../../wit/pathland.wit) — the WIT component world

## Run tests

```bash
PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo test
```

## Run the GTK desktop demo (native, zero-copy shared ring)

```bash
PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo run -p pathland-gtk-demo
```

Requires GTK4 (`brew install gtk4` on macOS).

## Run the Java demo (cross-language, JNA over the native C-ABI shim + GTK renderer)

```bash
PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo build -p pathland-native -p pathland-gtk
cd ../java/pathland-demo && mvn -q -Dpathland.rust.target=<lib/rust/target/debug> compile exec:java
```

On macOS, GTK must run on the main thread: prefix the mvn command with
`MAVEN_OPTS="-XstartOnFirstThread"`.

The Java app uses a SwiftUI-like DSL, drives the Rust engine via the flat
`pathland_native_*` C ABI (no per-component wrappers), and renders through the
shared `pathland-gtk` renderer (in-process via JNA). It uses **no Swing and no
GTK APIs directly** — native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes through the
shared ring, and the host drains them via `pathland_native_drain_events`. Verify
headlessly with `-Dexec.mainClass=demo.DemoHeadless`.


## Build for wasm32 (browser projection only)

```bash
RUSTC=~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/rustc \
  cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
```

> The Homebrew `cargo` on PATH resolves a rustc without the wasm std. Use the
> rustup toolchain's rustc via `RUSTC=...` (or `rustup run stable cargo`).

## Engine example

The engine emits declarative structure (no rects). A signal changes a property;
the next `emit` writes only the delta opcodes.

```rust
use pathland_engine::Engine;
use pathland_opcode::{init_memory, Guest, MemoryLayout};
use pathland_view::{assign_ids, text, vstack, View, ViewExt};

let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);

let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);
let mut engine = Engine::new();

let mut root = vstack![text("Hello")]
    .spacing(4.0)
    .padding(8.0)
    .build();
assign_ids(&mut root, &mut 1);

guest.begin_frame();
engine.emit(&root, &mut guest).unwrap(); // full structure
guest.end_frame();

root.properties.insert(pathland_opcode::property_id::SPACING, 12.0f32.to_bits());

guest.begin_frame();
engine.emit(&root, &mut guest).unwrap(); // exactly one SET_PROPERTY
guest.end_frame();
```

Emission in the steady state allocates nothing; only changed nodes produce
opcodes, so an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes. Native renderers map the
structure onto their native elements (GTK4 widgets, DOM elements).

## Network transport example

Frames emitted into the ring can be serialized into network batches and flushed
on a time/size policy (`BatchEncoder` / `Batcher`); a `BatchDecoder` rebuilds a
`Frame`-compatible view so the same `RenderTree::apply_frame` consumes batches
and shared-memory frames identically. See `spec/OPCODE.md#transport`.

<content>
1: # Pathland Protocol
2: 
3: > A cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol inspired by SwiftUI
4: 
5: ## Overview
6: 
7: Pathland is a **protocol-first** UI framework for **retained-mode UI** with
8: multiple renderer backends. It's inspired by SwiftUI's declarative syntax, but
9: designed to be **language-agnostic** and **platform-agnostic**.
10: 
11: As of August 2026 the core is a **Rust opcode engine**. It emits the
12: application's **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
13: padding, alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared
14: linear memory. Each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that
15: platform's **native elements** (GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the
16: browser, HTML server-side) and those native elements lay themselves out.
17: 
18: On desktop the engine runs **natively**: other languages drive it through the
19: flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-native`) over a zero-copy shared ring and render
20: through the shared GTK renderer (`pathland-gtk`). **WASM/WIT are the
21: browser/remote projection only**, not the primary path.
22: 
23: **The engine does not compute layout and does not emit rects.** It describes
24: *what* the UI is, never *where* it is. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**:
25: signals in the application ensure only changed nodes emit opcodes, so an
26: unchanged tree emits zero opcodes.
27: 
28: ## The Three Elements
29: 
30: Pathland is composed of three elements. They are the vocabulary the whole
31: project speaks, so they are settled and used consistently:
32: 
33: ```
34: ┌────────────────────┐        ┌─────────────────────┐
35: │ 1. Retained UI     │        │ 3. Renderer         │
36: │ the app's UI tree  │────┐   │ maps opcodes onto   │
37: │ (any language,     │    │   │ native elements +   │
38: │  any platform)     │    │   │ event reporting     │
39: └────────────────────┘    │   └───────────▲─────────┘
40:                          │                │
41: ┌────────────────────┐    │                │
42: │ 2. Opcode engine   │◄───┘                │
43: │ diffs + emits      │─────────────────────┘
44: └────────────────────┘
45: ```
46: 
47: 1. **Retained UI** — the application's canonical retained UI tree. It is the
48:    single source of truth, owned by the application. It can be authored in
49:    **any language on any platform**: Rust, Java, Swift, C#, C, TypeScript —
50:    desktop, mobile, embedded, or web — through a generated DSL, a WIT binding,
51:    or the flat native C ABI.
52: 2. **Opcode engine** — walks the retained tree, diffs it, and emits fixed
53:    **16-byte opcodes** (the producer). Emission is reactive: only changed nodes
54:    emit, so an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes. The engine is
55:    language-independent — the same opcode stream serves every renderer.
56: 3. **Renderer** — consumes the opcode stream and maps it onto that platform's
57:    **native elements**, and reports raw inputs back as events. It is a pure
58:    function of the opcode stream (stateless) and never retains application
59:    state. *"Host" and "driver" are roles a renderer plays: it runs inside a
60:    host and is pumped by a driver — they are not separate elements.* The same
61:    opcode stream targets **different UI systems**: a GTK4 renderer on desktop,
62:    an AppKit/SwiftUI renderer on macOS, a WinUI renderer on Windows, an LVGL
63:    renderer on embedded, a DOM renderer in the browser.
64: 
65: The opcodes are carried from the engine to the renderer by a transport (a
66: zero-copy shared-memory ring on desktop/native, a serialized network batch for
67: remote/browser); transport is an implementation detail, not a fourth element.
68: 
69: ## Core Principles
70: 
71: - **Protocol-first**: standardized, open protocol for UI components, events, and raw inputs
72: - **16-byte opcodes**: every instruction is a fixed 16 bytes — cache-line aligned, deterministic, linear decode
73: - **Declarative, not positioned**: the engine emits structure + constraint properties (spacing, padding, alignment); native renderers compute positions
74: - **Native elements everywhere**: GTK4 widgets, DOM elements, HTML — never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent
75: - **Reactive emission**: only the nodes that changed emit opcodes; steady state emits zero
76: - **Command-based**: UI updates are tree mutations (CREATE_NODE, DELETE_NODE, INSERT_CHILD, MOVE_CHILD, …), never serialized trees
77: - **Stateless renderers**: renderers are pure functions of the opcode stream; they retain only their own rendered output, never application state
78: - **Zero-copy**: ring and arena are plain regions of shared linear memory
79: - **Single-producer / single-consumer**: guest engine produces; host renderer consumes
80: - **Catalog-driven DSL**: the ergonomic SwiftUI-like DSL in any language is generated from a single YAML catalog (`lib/ui/`), not hand-written
81: 
82: ## Documentation
83: 
84: ### Specification

display.text:
# Pathland Protocol

> A cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol inspired by SwiftUI

## Overview

Pathland is a **protocol-first** UI framework for **retained-mode UI** with
multiple renderer backends. It's inspired by SwiftUI's declarative syntax, but
designed to be **language-agnostic** and **platform-agnostic**.

As of August 2026 the core is a **Rust opcode engine**. It emits the
application's **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
padding, alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared
linear memory. Each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that
platform's **native elements** (GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the
browser, HTML server-side) and those native elements lay themselves out.

On desktop the engine runs **natively**: other languages drive it through the
flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-native`) over a zero-copy shared ring and render
through the shared GTK renderer (`pathland-gtk`). **WASM/WIT are the
browser/remote projection only**, not the primary path.

**The engine does not compute layout and does not emit rects.** It describes
*what* the UI is, never *where* it is. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**:
signals in the application ensure only changed nodes emit opcodes, so an
unchanged tree emits zero opcodes.

## The Three Elements

Pathland is composed of three elements. They are the vocabulary the whole
project speaks, so they are settled and used consistently:

```
┌────────────────────┐        ┌─────────────────────┐
│ 1. Retained UI     │        │ 3. Renderer         │
│ the app's UI tree  │────┐   │ maps opcodes onto   │
│ (any language,     │    │   │ native elements +   │
│  any platform)     │    │   │ event reporting     │
└────────────────────┘    │   └───────────▲─────────┘
                         │                │
┌────────────────────┐    │                │
│ 2. Opcode engine   │◄───┘                │
│ diffs + emits      │─────────────────────┘
└────────────────────┘
```

1. **Retained UI** — the application's canonical retained UI tree. It is the
   single source of truth, owned by the application. It can be authored in
   **any language on any platform**: Rust, Java, Swift, C#, C, TypeScript —
   desktop, mobile, embedded, or web — through a generated DSL, a WIT binding,
   or the flat native C ABI.
2. **Opcode engine** — walks the retained tree, diffs it, and emits fixed
   **16-byte opcodes** (the producer). Emission is reactive: only changed nodes
   emit, so an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes. The engine is
   language-independent — the same opcode stream serves every renderer.
3. **Renderer** — consumes the opcode stream and maps it onto that platform's
   **native elements**, and reports raw inputs back as events. It is a pure
   function of the opcode stream (stateless) and never retains application
   state. *"Host" and "driver" are roles a renderer plays: it runs inside a
   host and is pumped by a driver — they are not separate elements.* The same
   opcode stream targets **different UI systems**: a GTK4 renderer on desktop,
   an AppKit/SwiftUI renderer on macOS, a WinUI renderer on Windows, an LVGL
   renderer on embedded, a DOM renderer in the browser.

The opcodes are carried from the engine to the renderer by a transport (a
zero-copy shared-memory ring on desktop/native, a serialized network batch for
remote/browser); transport is an implementation detail, not a fourth element.

## Core Principles

- **Protocol-first**: standardized, open protocol for UI components, events, and raw inputs
- **16-byte opcodes**: every instruction is a fixed 16 bytes — cache-line aligned, deterministic, linear decode
- **Declarative, not positioned**: the engine emits structure + constraint properties (spacing, padding, alignment); native renderers compute positions
- **Native elements everywhere**: GTK4 widgets, DOM elements, HTML — never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent
- **Reactive emission**: only the nodes that changed emit opcodes; steady state emits zero
- **Command-based**: UI updates are tree mutations (CREATE_NODE, DELETE_NODE, INSERT_CHILD, MOVE_CHILD, …), never serialized trees
- **Stateless renderers**: renderers are pure functions of the opcode stream; they retain only their own rendered output, never application state
- **Zero-copy**: ring and arena are plain regions of shared linear memory
- **Single-producer / single-consumer**: guest engine produces; host renderer consumes
- **Catalog-driven DSL**: the ergonomic SwiftUI-like DSL in any language is generated from a single YAML catalog (`lib/ui/`), not hand-written

## Documentation

### Specification

- [Opcode Protocol](./spec/OPCODE.md) — **Primary specification** — fixed 16-byte opcodes, ring buffer, arena, reactive emission, design tokens
- [Conformance Test Vectors](./spec/CONFORMANCE.md) — golden byte arrays for validating implementations

## Rust Workspace

The implementation is under [`lib/rust/`](./lib/rust/):

| Crate | Responsibility |
|-------|----------------|
| `pathland-opcode` | 16-byte opcode, ring buffer, bump arena, linear-memory layout (`no_std`) |
| `pathland-view` | SwiftUI-style view DSL: VStack/HStack/Text/Button + chainable modifiers (`no_std`) |
| `pathland-engine` | Retained view tree → declarative `TREE`/`STYLE` opcodes; diff-based reactive emission (zero-alloc steady state) |
| `pathland-host` | Host reader: ring → native-element description (`std` convenience layer) |
| `pathland-transport` | Opcode transport: shared-memory ring + network batch encode/decode + transport abstraction |
| `pathland-native` | Native C-ABI shim + `NativeHost`: flat world over a zero-copy shared ring (Swift/Java/C#…) |
| `pathland-gtk` | GTK4 renderer (rlib + cdylib): opcode frames → native GTK widgets, incrementally |
| `pathland-gtk-demo` | Rust GTK4 demo: authors the DSL, renders through `pathland-gtk` (no GTK APIs) |
| `pathland-codegen` | DSL code generator: parses `lib/ui/components.yaml`, asserts ids, emits the Java DSL |
| `pathland-guest` | WASM guest component (browser/remote only) |
| `pathland-wit-host` | WIT host bindings + DSL bridge (browser/remote only) |

The DSL catalog lives in [`lib/ui/components.yaml`](./lib/ui/components.yaml);
regenerate the Java DSL with `./generate.sh`.

### Run tests

```bash
cd lib/rust
cargo test
```

### Run the demos (native, zero-copy shared ring + GTK renderer)

```bash
# Rust demo
cd lib/rust && PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo run -p pathland-gtk-demo

# Java demo (JNA over pathland-native + pathland-gtk)
PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo build -p pathland-native -p pathland-gtk
cd lib/java/pathland-demo && mvn -q -Dpathland.rust.target=<lib/rust/target/debug> compile exec:java
```

On macOS the Java demo must run GTK on the main thread:
`MAVEN_OPTS="-XstartOnFirstThread"`.

### Build for wasm32 (browser projection only)

```bash
RUSTC=~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/rustc \
  cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
```

## Components & Properties

Component and property IDs are defined in `pathland-opcode`'s
[`constants.rs`](./lib/rust/crates/pathland-opcode/src/constants.rs) and
documented in [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md). Component types include `HSTACK`,
`VSTACK`, `TEXT`, `BUTTON`, `SPACER`, and more; stack constraint properties
(`SPACING`, `ALIGNMENT`, …) drive native layout, styling modifiers (`PADDING`,
`COLOR`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, …) decorate any view, and `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`
use `-1` = FILL, `-2` = HUG_CONTENT.

## Design Tokens

The renderer owns default token values; the application owns overrides.
Tokens are identified by dot-separated paths (`color.primary`, `space.2`) and
referenced via the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type or overridden globally with
`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`. See [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system).

## Roadmap (POC Goals)

See the GitHub issues (#12, #13, #15, #16, #18):

1. **16-byte opcode engine** — done
2. **Core components & modifiers in Rust** (SwiftUI-like API) — done
3. **Opcode transport layer** (shared memory + network batch + native C-ABI shim) — done
4. **Rust desktop app with GTK4 renderer** (native shared ring) — done
5. **Catalog-driven DSL** (YAML → Java via `pathland-codegen`) — done
6. Quarkus SSR + WebSocket demo — planned

## Versioning

Pathland follows **Semantic Versioning** (Major.Minor.Patch). The wire protocol
version is 1 (see [OPCODE.md](./spec/OPCODE.md)).

## License

Pathland is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details.

Now I have a good picture. Let me understand the mapping to the 3 elements and read key lib.rs files to understand the roles and how they interrelate. Let me read the lib.rs of pathland-host, pathland-transport/lib.rs, pathland-native/lib.rs, pathland-gtk/lib.rs, pathland-engine/lib.rs, pathland-view/lib.rs briefly.

Let me focus on understanding:
- What is the "retained UI model"? That's pathland-view (the DSL produces a retained view tree) + the Node tree. Actually retained UI = the app's UI tree. In Rust, the retained tree is `pathland-view`'s `Node` tree (built by DSL). The engine walks it.
- Opcode engine = pathland-opcode (the opcode format) + pathland-engine (diff emission). Also transport.
- Renderer = pathland-host (native element description) + pathland-gtk (GTK). Also pathland-native is a host/driver.

Let me read the key lib.rs docs to understand boundaries.

1: //! # pathland-host
2: //!
3: //! Host-side reader for the Pathland 16-byte opcode ring. Consumes frames from
4: //! shared linear memory and builds a **native-element description**: the tree
5: //! structure (`TREE`) plus constraint properties (`STYLE`) a renderer maps onto
6: //! that platform's native elements (GTK widgets, DOM elements, HTML).
7: //!
8: //! The engine does not compute layout; this crate stores only what the renderer
9: //! needs to create native elements and let them lay themselves out.
10: 
11: use std::collections::HashMap;
12: 
13: pub use pathland_engine;
14: pub use pathland_opcode;
15: 
16: use pathland_opcode::category;
17: use pathland_opcode::component_type;
18: use pathland_opcode::style;
19: use pathland_opcode::tree;
20: use pathland_opcode::{Frame, Opcode};
21: 
22: /// A decoded node in the host's native-element description.
23: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
24: pub struct HostNode {
25:     pub id: u32,
26:     pub component_type: u16,
27:     pub text: Option<String>,
28:     pub parent: Option<u32>,
29:     pub children: Vec<u32>,
30:     /// Constraint properties (propertyId → value) for native layout/styling.
31:     pub properties: HashMap<u16, u32>,
32: }
33: 
34: impl Default for HostNode {
35:     fn default() -> Self {
36:         Self {
37:             id: 0,
38:             component_type: component_type::HSTACK,
39:             text: None,
40:             parent: None,
41:             children: Vec::new(),
42:             properties: HashMap::new(),
43:         }
44:     }
45: }
46: 
47: /// The host's native-element description of a rendered tree.
48: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
49: pub struct RenderTree {
50:     /// nodeId → node.
51:     pub nodes: HashMap<u32, HostNode>,
52: }
53: 
54: impl RenderTree {
55:     /// Apply a frame's opcodes to this tree (a delta).
56:     pub fn apply_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame<'_>) {
57:         for op in frame.opcodes() {
58:             match (op.category(), op.command()) {
59:                 (category::TREE, tree::CREATE_NODE) => {
60:                     let id = op.a();
61:                     let ty = op.b() as u16;
62:                     let entry = self.nodes.entry(id).or_default();
63:                     entry.id = id;
64:                     entry.component_type = ty;
65:                 }
66:                 (category::TREE, tree::DELETE_NODE) => {
67:                     self.nodes.remove(&op.a());
68:                 }
69:                 (category::TREE, tree::INSERT_CHILD) => {
70:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
71:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
72:                         if !p.children.contains(&child) {
73:                             p.children.push(child);
74:                         }
75:                     }
76:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
77:                         c.parent = Some(parent);
78:                     }
79:                 }
80:                 (category::TREE, tree::REMOVE_CHILD) => {
81:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
82:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
83:                         p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);
84:                     }
85:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
86:                         c.parent = None;
87:                     }
88:                 }
89:                 (category::TREE, tree::MOVE_CHILD) => {
90:                     let (parent, child, new_index) = (op.a(), op.b(), op.c() as usize);
91:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
92:                         if let Some(pos) = p.children.iter().position(|c| *c == child) {
93:                             p.children.remove(pos);
94:                         }
95:                         let idx = if new_index == usize::MAX {
96:                             p.children.len()
97:                         } else {
98:                             new_index.min(p.children.len())
99:                         };
100:                         p.children.insert(idx, child);
101:                     }
102:                 }
103:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_PROPERTY) => {
104:                     let prop_id = op.b() as u16;
105:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
106:                         n.properties.insert(prop_id, op.c());
107:                     }
108:                 }
109:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_TEXT) => {
110:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
111:                         n.text = frame.arena_str(op.b()).ok().map(|s| s.to_string());
112:                     }
113:                 }
114:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN) => {
115:                     // Token overrides are handled by the renderer's theme layer.
116:                     let _ = op;
117:                 }
118:                 _ => {}
119:             }
120:         }
121:     }
122: 
123:     /// Look up a node by id.
124:     pub fn node(&self, id: u32) -> Option<&HostNode> {
125:         self.nodes.get(&id)
126:     }
127: 
128:     /// The root node: the single node without a parent.
129:     pub fn root(&self) -> Option<&HostNode> {
130:         self.nodes.values().find(|n| n.parent.is_none())
131:     }
132: }

136:     let mut tree = RenderTree::default();
137:     tree.apply_frame(frame);
138:     tree
139: }

1: //! # pathland-transport
2: //!
3: //! How Pathland opcodes are transported from the guest engine to host
4: //! renderers. There are two peer backends:
5: //!
6: //! - **Shared memory** (desktop/native): the ring buffer + arena in
7: //!   `pathland-opcode` (`Guest`/`Host`). Zero-copy. This crate treats it as
8: //!   the local transport — no duplication.
9: //! - **Network batch** (SSR → browser): opcodes + arena data serialized into
10: //!   **batches**, flushed on a **time interval** or a **network-frame size**
11: //!   (whichever comes first).
12: //!
13: //! `pathland_opcode::Frame` is the **transport seam**: `pathland-host`'s
14: //! `RenderTree::apply_frame` consumes frames regardless of origin. `BatchDecoder`
15: //! produces `Frame` views over decoded batches, so a network batch feeds the
16: //! renderer exactly like a shared-memory frame.
17: //!
18: //! ## Batch wire format
19: //!
20: //! ```text
21: //! magic "PLPL" (u32 LE) | version (u16) | flags (u16) | frameCount (u32)
22: //! | opcodeCount (u32) | opcodes (16 B × opcodeCount) | arenaDeltaLen (u32)
23: //! | arena delta bytes
24: //! ```
25: //!
26: //! The arena is append-only (bump); batches carry only the bytes appended since
27: //! the previous batch. The decoder appends them to a mirrored arena, so absolute
28: //! `arenaRef` offsets stay valid — exactly as in shared memory.
29: //!
30: //! ## Example (producer)
31: //!
32: //! ```no_run
33: //! use pathland_transport::{Batcher, BatchPolicy, BatchEncoder};
34: //! use std::time::Duration;
35: //!
36: //! let policy = BatchPolicy::new(Duration::from_millis(4), 1400);
37: //! let mut batcher = Batcher::new(policy);
38: //! let mut encoder = BatchEncoder::new();
39: //!
40: //! // batcher.push_frame(&frame) accumulates opcodes + arena delta;
41: //! // batcher.flush() -> Option<Vec<u8>> produces the serialized batch.
42: //! ```
43: 
44: #![forbid(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]
45: 
46: extern crate alloc;
47: 
48: mod batch;
49: mod batching;
50: mod conformance;
51: mod net;
52: mod ring;
53: mod traits;
54: 
55: pub use batch::{encode_batch, Batch, BatchDecoder, BatchEncoder};
56: pub use batching::{Batcher, BatchPolicy};
57: pub use net::NetBatchEncoder;
58: pub use ring::RingTransport;
59: pub use traits::{
60:     DriverTransport, FrameSource, InputSink, OpcodeBatch, ProtocolError, TransportError,
61: };
62: 
63: /// Wire magic for network batches (`PLPL`).
64: pub const BATCH_MAGIC: u32 = 0x504C_504C;
65: /// Wire version for the batch format.
66: pub const BATCH_VERSION: u16 = 1;
67:

69: pub mod direction {
70:     /// The batch carries guest → host tree/style opcodes.
71:     pub const GUEST_TO_HOST: u16 = 0x0000;
72:     /// The batch carries host → guest raw-input events (reserved).
73:     pub const HOST_TO_GUEST: u16 = 0x0001;

1: //! # pathland-native
2: //!
3: //! Native (non-WASM) projection of the Pathland flat world, exposed over both a
4: //! Rust API and a C ABI for foreign host languages (Swift / Java / C# / …).
5: //!
6: //! This is the **cross-language, zero-copy** path: a host links this crate as a
7: //! native library (or a `cdylib` and its `pathland_native_*` C functions), drives
8: //! the retained tree with the flat `builder`/`engine` operations, and reads
9: //! opcodes from the **shared-memory ring in place** — no serialization, no batch,
10: //! no WASM.
11: //!
12: //! The surface mirrors `wit/pathland.wit` (`builder`, `engine`) but for a native
13: //! shared-memory transport instead of a WASM/WIT ABI.
14: 
15: use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};
16: 
17: use pathland_engine::Engine;
18: use pathland_opcode::{component_type, property_id, MemoryLayout};
19: use pathland_transport::{
20:     DriverTransport, FrameSource, OpcodeBatch, RingTransport, TransportError,
21: };
22: use pathland_view::{component_type_id, Node};

24: mod capi;

26: /// A flat node in the host's retained tree (id → node).
27: #[derive(Clone)]
28: pub struct FlatNode {
29:     pub id: u32,
30:     pub view_component: pathland_view::Component,
31:     pub properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,
32:     pub parent: Option<u32>,
33:     pub children: Vec<u32>,
34: }
35: 
36: /// The native host: owns the retained tree, the diff engine, and the shared
37: /// zero-copy ring.
38: pub struct NativeHost {
39:     nodes: HashMap<u32, FlatNode>,
40:     engine: Engine,
41:     ring: RingTransport,
42: }
43: 
44: /// Safe, checked operations returning `()` (used by the C shim).
45: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
46: pub enum HostError {
47:     /// The operation referenced a missing node.
48:     NotFound,
49: }
50: 
51: impl NativeHost {
52:     /// Create a host with a fresh shared ring (default layout).
53:     pub fn new() -> Self {
54:         Self {
55:             nodes: HashMap::new(),
56:             engine: Engine::new(),
57:             ring: RingTransport::new(),
58:         }
59:     }
60: 
61:     /// Create a host over a caller-provided ring buffer + layout.
62:     pub fn with_buffer(mem: Vec<u8>, layout: MemoryLayout) -> Self {
63:         Self {
64:             nodes: HashMap::new(),
65:             engine: Engine::new(),
66:             ring: RingTransport::with_buffer(mem, layout),
67:         }
68:     }
69: 
70:     /// Create (or reset) a node with a host-supplied stable id.
71:     pub fn create_node(&mut self, id: u32, component: pathland_view::Component) {
72:         let entry = self.nodes.entry(id).or_insert(FlatNode {
73:             id,
74:             view_component: component.clone(),
75:             properties: BTreeMap::new(),
76:             parent: None,
77:             children: Vec::new(),
78:         });
79:         entry.view_component = component;
80:         entry.properties.clear();
81:     }
82: 
83:     /// Insert `child` into `parent` at `index` (u32::MAX appends).
84:     pub fn insert_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32, index: u32) {
85:         if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
86:             let idx = if index == u32::MAX {
87:                 p.children.len()
88:             } else {
89:                 (index as usize).min(p.children.len())
90:             };
91:             if !p.children.contains(&child) {
92:                 p.children.insert(idx, child);
93:             }
94:         }
95:         if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
96:             c.parent = Some(parent);
97:         }
98:     }
99: 
100:     /// Remove `child` from `parent`.
101:     pub fn remove_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32) {
102:         if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
103:             p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);
104:         }
105:         if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
106:             c.parent = None;
107:         }
108:     }
109: 
110:     /// Set a node's text content.
111:     pub fn set_text(&mut self, id: u32, text: &str) {
112:         if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&id) {
113:             match &mut node.view_component {
114:                 pathland_view::Component::Text { text: t } => *t = text.into(),
115:                 pathland_view::Component::Button { label } => *label = text.into(),
116:                 _ => {}
117:             }
118:         }
119:     }
120: 
121:     /// Set a constraint/style property (raw value bits; valueType derived from
122:     /// the property id).
123:     pub fn set_property(&mut self, id: u32, prop: u16, value: u32) {
124:         if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&id) {
125:             node.properties.insert(prop, value);
126:         }
127:     }
128: 
129:     /// Set a float property (stores `f32` bit pattern).
130:     pub fn set_property_f32(&mut self, id: u32, prop: u16, value: f32) {
131:         self.set_property(id, prop, value.to_bits());
132:     }
133: 
134:     /// Emit the retained tree as opcodes into the shared ring.
135:     ///
136:     /// Returns `true` if a frame was written (i.e. the tree is non-empty).
137:     pub fn emit(&mut self) -> bool {
138:         let root = self.root_id().and_then(|r| self.materialize(r));
139:         if let Some(root) = root {
140:             let mut guest = self.ring.producer();
141:             guest.begin_frame();
142:             let _ = self.engine.emit(&root, &mut guest);
143:             guest.end_frame();
144:             true
145:         } else {
146:             false
147:         }
148:     }
149: 
150:     /// The ring's linear-memory buffer (for embedding / FFI).
151:     pub fn ring_buffer(&self) -> &[u8] {
152:         self.ring.buffer()
153:     }
154: 
155:     /// Consume the ring transport (for hosts that read frames via `FrameSource`).
156:     pub fn take_ring(self) -> RingTransport {
157:         self.ring
158:     }
159: 
160:     /// The ring memory layout (region geometry).
161:     pub fn layout(&self) -> MemoryLayout {
162:         *self.layout_ref()
163:     }
164: 
165:     fn layout_ref(&self) -> &MemoryLayout {
166:         self.ring.layout()
167:     }
168: 
169:     /// The single node without a parent (the root).
170:     pub fn root_id(&self) -> Option<u32> {
171:         self.nodes.values().find(|n| n.parent.is_none()).map(|n| n.id)
172:     }
173: 
174:     /// Materialize a `pathland_view::Node` subtree rooted at `id`.
175:     fn materialize(&self, id: u32) -> Option<Node> {
176:         let flat = self.nodes.get(&id)?.clone();
177:         let mut node = Node::from_component(&flat.view_component);
178:         node.id = flat.id;
179:         node.properties = flat.properties.clone();
180:         for child_id in &flat.children {
181:             if let Some(child) = self.materialize(*child_id) {
182:                 node.children.push(child);
183:             }
184:         }
185:         Some(node)
186:     }
187: }

189: impl Default for NativeHost {
190:     fn default() -> Self {
191:         Self::new()
192:     }
193: }
194: 
195: /// The host is a `FrameSource` over its shared ring: a renderer drains the
196: /// guest→host frames the engine produced.
197: impl FrameSource for NativeHost {
198:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
199:         self.ring.next_frame()

204: impl DriverTransport for NativeHost {

206:         self.ring.send_input(event)

208: }

211:     /// Drain raw-input events written by a renderer into the host → guest event
212:     /// ring (guest side). The application polls this to receive inputs.
213:     pub fn drain_events(&mut self) -> Vec<pathland_opcode::Event> {
214:         self.ring.drain_events()

219: ///
220: /// Mirrors the `component` variant values: hstack=1, vstack=2, text=3,
221: /// button=4, spacer=8.
222: pub fn component_from_id(id: u32) -> Option<pathland_view::Component> {
223:     match id {
224:         x if x == component_type::HSTACK as u32 => Some(pathland_view::Component::HStack),
225:         x if x == component_type::VSTACK as u32 => Some(pathland_view::Component::VStack),
226:         x if x == component_type::TEXT as u32 => {
227:             Some(pathland_view::Component::Text { text: String::new() })
228:         }
229:         x if x == component_type::BUTTON as u32 => {
230:             Some(pathland_view::Component::Button { label: String::new() })
231:         }
232:         x if x == component_type::SPACER as u32 => Some(pathland_view::Component::Spacer),
233:         _ => None,
234:     }

236: 
237: /// Map a component to its raw u32 id (C ABI).
238: pub fn component_id(component: &pathland_view::Component) -> u32 {

253:     } else {

1: //! # pathland-engine
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland **guest engine**. It holds the application's **retained view
4: //! tree** (built with the SwiftUI-style DSL in `pathland-view`) and emits the
5: //! **declarative structure** as `TREE`/`STYLE` opcodes into the 16-byte ring
6: //! buffer — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment. It does **not**
7: //! compute rects or layout; native renderers (GTK4 widgets, DOM flexbox) lay
8: //! out their own native elements from these constraints.
9: //!
10: //! ## Reactive emission
11: //!
12: //! Emission is **diff-based**: on each `emit` the engine compares the current
13: //! tree against a snapshot of what it last emitted, and writes only the
14: //! opcodes for nodes that actually changed. An unchanged tree emits **zero**
15: //! opcodes. This is what signals in the application drive — a signal marks the
16: //! tree dirty; `emit` reconciles.
17: //!
18: //! Both **property diffs** (`SET_PROPERTY`, `SET_TEXT`) and **structural diffs**
19: //! (`CREATE_NODE`, `DELETE_NODE`, `INSERT_CHILD`, `REMOVE_CHILD`, `MOVE_CHILD`)
20: //! are emitted.
21: //!
22: //! ## Zero allocation
23: //!
24: //! The emit pass performs **zero dynamic heap allocations** in the steady
25: //! state. The snapshot is a preallocated slab indexed by node id; per-pass
26: //! bookkeeping uses generation stamps instead of rebuilding maps. Allocations
27: //! only occur when the tree *grows* (new nodes resize the slab) or a node's
28: //! property set actually changes.
29: 
30: #![no_std]
31: #![forbid(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]
32: 
33: #[cfg(test)]
34: extern crate std;
35: 
36: extern crate alloc;

39: use alloc::collections::BTreeMap;
40: use alloc::string::String;
41: use alloc::vec::Vec;

43: use pathland_opcode::Guest;
44: use pathland_view::{component_type_id, value_type_for, Node};
45: 
46: pub use pathland_opcode;
47: pub use pathland_view;
48: 
49: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
50: // Retained view tree (from pathland-view)
51: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
52: 
53: pub use pathland_view::{Component, View, ViewModifier};
54: 
55: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
56: // Snapshot (previous emitted state)
57: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
58: 
59: /// Per-node state the engine remembers from the last emission.
60: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
61: struct SnapshotNode {
62:     component_type: u16,
63:     parent: Option<u32>,
64:     index: usize,
65:     text: Option<String>,
66:     properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,
67:     /// Generation stamp set on each emit pass; used to detect deleted nodes.
68:     gen: u64,
69: }
70: 
71: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
72: // Engine
73: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
74: 
75: /// Result of an emission pass.
76: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
77: pub struct EmitResult {
78:     /// Number of opcodes written to the ring.
79:     pub opcodes: usize,
80: }
81: 
82: /// The diff-based reactive emitter.
83: ///
84: /// `Engine` keeps the snapshot of what was last emitted. Calling `emit` with a
85: /// (possibly mutated) retained tree writes only the delta opcodes. The steady
86: /// state of the emit pass allocates nothing.
87: pub struct Engine {
88:     /// nodeId → last emitted state (a preallocated slab; node ids are dense).
89:     snapshot: Vec<Option<SnapshotNode>>,
90:     /// Monotonic generation stamp for the current pass.
91:     gen: u64,
92: }
93: 
94: impl Default for Engine {
95:     fn default() -> Self {
96:         Self::new()
97:     }
98: }
99: 
100: impl Engine {
101:     pub fn new() -> Self {
102:         Self {
103:             snapshot: Vec::new(),
104:             gen: 0,
105:         }
106:     }
107: 
108:     /// Reconcile `root` against the snapshot, emitting only changed opcodes.
109:     pub fn emit(
110:         &mut self,
111:         root: &Node,
112:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
113:     ) -> Result<EmitResult, pathland_opcode::RingError> {
114:         self.gen = self.gen.wrapping_add(1);
115:         let mut out = 0usize;
116:         self.reconcile_node(root, None, 0, guest, &mut out)?;
117: 
118:         // Delete any node that existed in the snapshot but was not visited this
119:         // pass (generation stamp unchanged).
120:         for (id, slot) in self.snapshot.iter_mut().enumerate() {
121:             if let Some(s) = slot {
122:                 if s.gen != self.gen {
123:                     guest.delete_node(id as u32)?;
124:                     out += 1;
125:                     *slot = None;
126:                 }
127:             }
128:         }
129:         Ok(EmitResult { opcodes: out })
130:     }
131: 
132:     /// Number of nodes tracked in the snapshot (diagnostics).
133:     pub fn tracked_nodes(&self) -> usize {
134:         self.snapshot.iter().filter(|s| s.is_some()).count()
135:     }

137:     fn slot_mut(&mut self, id: u32) -> &mut Option<SnapshotNode> {
138:         let idx = id as usize;
139:         if self.snapshot.len() <= idx {
140:             self.snapshot.resize(idx + 1, None);
141:         }
142:         &mut self.snapshot[idx]
143:     }

145:     #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
146:     fn reconcile_node(
147:         &mut self,
148:         node: &Node,
149:         parent: Option<u32>,
150:         index: usize,
151:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
152:         out: &mut usize,
153:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_opcode::RingError> {
154:         let component_type = component_type_id(&node.component);
155: 
156:         let text_borrowed = match &node.component {
157:             Component::Text { text } => Some(text.as_str()),
158:             Component::Button { label } => Some(label.as_str()),
159:             _ => None,
160:         };
161: 
162:         let prev = self.slot_mut(node.id).take();
163:         let props_changed = match &prev {
164:             Some(p) => p.properties != node.properties,
165:             None => !node.properties.is_empty(),
166:         };
167:         // Text is owned in the snapshot; compare without cloning.
168:         let text_changed = match &prev {
169:             Some(p) => p.text.as_deref() != text_borrowed,
170:             None => text_borrowed.is_some(),
171:         };
172: 
173:         match &prev {
174:             // New node: CREATE_NODE + INSERT_CHILD + all properties/text.
175:             None => {
176:                 guest.create_node(node.id, component_type)?;
177:                 *out += 1;
178:                 if let Some(p) = parent {
179:                     guest.insert_child(p, node.id, index as u32)?;
180:                     *out += 1;
181:                 }
182:                 for (prop, value) in &node.properties {
183:                     guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type_for(*prop), *value)?;
184:                     *out += 1;
185:                 }
186:                 if let Some(t) = text_borrowed {
187:                     guest.set_text(node.id, t)?;
188:                     *out += 1;
189:                 }
190:             }
191:             Some(p) => {
192:                 // Structural changes.
193:                 if p.parent != parent {
194:                     if let Some(old) = p.parent {
195:                         guest.remove_child(old, node.id)?;
196:                         *out += 1;
197:                     }
198:                     if let Some(new) = parent {
199:                         guest.insert_child(new, node.id, index as u32)?;

201:                     }
202:                 } else if p.index != index {
203:                     if let Some(par) = parent {
204:                         guest.move_child(par, node.id, index as u32)?;
205:                         *out += 1;
206:                     }
207:                 }
208:                 // Component type changed → recreate.
209:                 if p.component_type != component_type {
210:                     guest.create_node(node.id, component_type)?;
211:                     *out += 1;
212:                 }
213:                 // Text diff.
214:                 if text_changed {
215:                     if let Some(t) = text_borrowed {
216:                         guest.set_text(node.id, t)?;
217:                         *out += 1;
218:                     }

2: //!
3: //! The producer (opcode engine) and consumer (native driver) share one linear
4: //! memory buffer containing the ring + arena. The producer writes 16-byte
5: //! opcodes via `pathland_opcode::Guest`; the consumer reads completed frames via
6: //! `pathland_opcode::Host`. No copying, no batching, no serialization — this is
7: //! the high-performance local path.

9: use pathland_opcode::{init_memory, Guest, Host, MemoryLayout};

11: use crate::traits::{DriverTransport, FrameSource, OpcodeBatch, TransportError};

13: /// A zero-copy SPSC shared-memory ring transport.
14: ///
15: /// Owns the linear-memory buffer (header + ring + arena). Producers and
16: /// consumers are granted short-lived `Guest`/`Host` views over the same buffer
17: /// via the borrowed methods, so opcodes flow in place with no copies.
18: #[derive(Debug)]
19: pub struct RingTransport {
20:     /// Shared linear memory (header | ring | arena).
21:     mem: Vec<u8>,
22:     /// Ring/arena geometry.
23:     layout: MemoryLayout,
24: }

26: impl RingTransport {
27:     /// Create a ring transport with a default layout and a zeroed header.
28:     pub fn new() -> Self {
29:         let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
30:         let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
31:         init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
32:         Self { mem, layout }
33:     }
34:

48:     /// consumer must not overlap borrows.

display.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build and run the Pathland Java demo (JNA over pathland-native + GTK renderer).
#
# Usage:
#   ./run.sh                 # run demo.GtkDemo
#   ./run.sh demo.DemoHeadless   # run the headless verification demo
#
# The Rust native libs (libpathland_native, libpathland_gtk) are built first,
# then the Java is compiled and launched with `java` directly (NOT
# `mvn exec:java`) — on macOS GTK must run on the process's main thread, which
# requires `-XstartOnFirstThread` on the `java` invocation; the Maven exec
# plugin does not propagate that flag correctly.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.." && pwd)"
RUST_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/lib/rust"
RUST_TARGET="$RUST_DIR/target/debug"
DEMO_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/lib/java/pathland-demo"

MAIN_CLASS="${1:-demo.GtkDemo}"

export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"

echo "==> Building native libs (pathland-native, pathland-gtk)"
(cd "$RUST_DIR" && cargo build -p pathland-native -p pathland-gtk)

echo "==> Compiling Java demo"
(cd "$DEMO_DIR" && mvn -q compile)

echo "==> Resolving Java classpath"
(cd "$DEMO_DIR" && mvn -q dependency:build-classpath \
    -Dmdep.outputFile="$DEMO_DIR/target/classpath.txt")

CLASSPATH="$DEMO_DIR/target/classes:$(cat "$DEMO_DIR/target/classpath.txt")"

JAVA_BIN="${JAVA_HOME:+$JAVA_HOME/bin/}java"

JVM_ARGS=()
if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Darwin" ]]; then
    # GTK must initialize on the main thread on macOS; the flag must be passed
    # to `java` itself (not via MAVEN_OPTS / mvn exec:java).
    JVM_ARGS+=("-XstartOnFirstThread")
fi

echo "==> Running $MAIN_CLASS"
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH="$RUST_TARGET${DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH}" \
    "$JAVA_BIN" "${JVM_ARGS[@]}" \
    -Djna.library.path="$RUST_TARGET" \
    -cp "$CLASSPATH" \
    "$MAIN_CLASS"

## Plan: Simplify the `lib/rust` crate structure

### Diagnosis — why it feels fragmented

The repo says the system has **three elements** (Retained UI, Opcode engine, Renderer), but the crate boundaries and names don't surface them. Mapping the 11 crates today:

| Element | Crates involved |
|---|---|
| 1. Retained UI | `pathland-view` (DSL + `Node` tree) |
| 2. Opcode engine | `pathland-opcode` (format/ring/arena) + `pathland-engine` (diff emit) + `pathland-transport` (carrier) |
| 3. Renderer | `pathland-host` (`RenderTree` decode) + `pathland-gtk` (native mapping) |
| Not an element (projection / demo / tool) | `pathland-guest`, `pathland-wit-host`, `pathland-native`, `pathland-gtk-demo`, `pathland-codegen` |

Two problems stand out:
1. **Element 2 is split across 3 crates**, and two crates both self-describe as "the engine" (`pathland-opcode`'s lib.rs literally says "the 16-byte opcode engine"; `pathland-engine` is the diff emitter).
2. **Thin layers exist only to be wired together**: `pathland-host` is 270 lines and its *only* production consumer is `pathland-gtk`; `pathland-transport`'s `ring.rs` (255 lines) just re-wraps `pathland-opcode`'s `Guest`/`Host`.

### Hard constraints (verified, not opinions)

These prevent a naive "3 crates = 3 elements" collapse:

- **Dependency cycle**: `opcode ← view ← engine` (`engine` needs `view::Node`; `view` needs `opcode` constants). You *cannot* merge `engine` into `opcode` without also merging `view`, which would erase the Element-1/Element-2 boundary.
- **`no_std` boundary**: `opcode`, `view`, `engine` are `no_std`; `transport` is `std` (uses `std::time::Duration`). Folding `transport` into the `no_std` core forces a `std` feature-gate or dropping `no_std`.
- **Crate-type locks**: `pathland-guest` (wasm32 component, WIT world), `pathland-native` (`cdylib` + `rlib`), `pathland-gtk` (`cdylib` + `rlib`, only place touching GTK) must stay separate.
- **External references to stable names**: `generate.sh` (`cargo run -p pathland-codegen`), `run.sh` (`cargo build -p pathland-native -p pathland-gtk`), and JNA symbols `pathland_native_*` / `pathland_gtk_*` (via `[lib] name`, not crate name — safe to rename crates as long as `[lib] name` stays).

### Recommended target structure (11 → 8 crates)

Three core libraries aligned to the elements, plus projections/demo/tool that are *clearly labeled* as such:

```
crates/
├── pathland-view/        # Element 1 — Retained UI (DSL + Node tree)   [no_std, unchanged]
├── pathland-opcode/      # Element 2 — Opcode engine (opcode format + ring + arena)
│                         #   + diff emitter (absorbs pathland-engine)
├── pathland-transport/   # Element 2 — transport (ring ownership + network batch)  [std, unchanged]
├── pathland-gtk/         # Element 3 — Renderer (absorbs pathland-host's RenderTree)
├── pathland-native/      # Projection — native C-ABI shim + NativeHost   [host/driver role]
├── pathland-guest/       # Projection — WASM component (browser/remote)
├── pathland-wit-host/    # Projection — wasmtime host bridge (browser/remote)
├── pathland-codegen/     # Tool — DSL generator (bin)
└── pathland-gtk-demo/    # Demo — bin
```

## Pathland `lib/rust` — Structure Simplification Plan

### Goal
Reduce 11 crates → 9, and make every library crate's name self-evidently map to one of the three elements: **Retained UI (`view`)**, **Opcode engine (`core`)**, **Renderer (`render`)**.

### Naming rules
- Retained UI → `pathland-view*`
- Opcode engine → `pathland-core*`
- Renderer → `pathland-render*`
- Tools/demos are exempt (they implement no element).

### Target structure

| # | New crate | Role | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `pathland-core` | Opcode engine: opcode + ring + arena + constants + events + `Node`/`Component` + diff emitter (`no_std`) | `pathland-opcode` + `pathland-engine` + tree types from `pathland-view` |
| 2 | `pathland-view` | Retained UI: DSL (`vstack!`, `hstack!`, `text`, modifiers, `TapRecognizer`) | `pathland-view` (tree types removed) |
| 3 | `pathland-core-transport` | Opcode engine: transport (ring owner + network batch, `std`) | `pathland-transport` |
| 4 | `pathland-render-gtk` | Renderer: `RenderTree` decode + GTK native mapping | `pathland-gtk` + `pathland-host` |
| 5 | `pathland-view-native` | Retained UI projection: C-ABI shim + `NativeHost` | `pathland-native` |
| 6 | `pathland-view-guest` | Retained UI projection: WASM guest component | `pathland-guest` |
| 7 | `pathland-view-wit` | Retained UI projection: wasmtime host bridge | `pathland-wit-host` |
| 8 | `pathland-codegen` | Tool (bin) — exempt, unchanged | `pathland-codegen` |
| 9 | `pathland-render-gtk-demo` | Demo (bin) — exempt | `pathland-gtk-demo` |

### Dependency graph (post-refactor)

```
pathland-core                    (no deps, no_std)
├── pathland-view                → core
├── pathland-core-transport      → core           (std)
├── pathland-render-gtk          → core + transport
├── pathland-view-native         → core + view + transport
├── pathland-view-guest          → core + view + transport   (wasm32)
├── pathland-view-wit            → core + view + transport
├── pathland-codegen             → core
└── pathland-render-gtk-demo     → core + view + transport + render-gtk
```

### Execution steps

1. **Create `pathland-core`**
   - Rename crate `pathland-opcode` → `pathland-core` (update `[package] name`, workspace members).
   - Move `pathland-engine/src/lib.rs` (`Engine`, `SnapshotNode`, `EmitResult`, diff tests) in as `engine.rs`.
   - Move `Node`, `Component`, `assign_ids`, `component_type_id`, `value_type_for` (+ their tests) from `pathland-view` into `core` (e.g. `tree.rs` / `component.rs`).
   - Re-export the public tree API so downstream `use` sites barely change.

2. **Trim `pathland-view`**
   - Remove the moved tree types; keep macros, `View`/`ViewModifier`, all modifiers, `Text`/`Stack` etc., `recognizer.rs`.
   - Add `pathland-core` dependency (replacing `pathland-opcode`); import `Node`/`Component`/constants from `pathland_core`.

3. **Merge `pathland-host` → `pathland-render-gtk`**
   - Rename crate `pathland-gtk` → `pathland-render-gtk`.
   - Move `host/src/lib.rs` (`HostNode`, `RenderTree`, `render_tree_from_frame`, `describe`) in as `host.rs`.
   - Retarget the three **dev-dependencies** (`native`, `wit-host`, `transport` tests) from `pathland-host` → `pathland-render-gtk` (or drop if test-only).

4. **Rename remaining crates**
   - `pathland-transport` → `pathland-core-transport`
   - `pathland-native` → `pathland-view-native`
   - `pathland-guest` → `pathland-view-guest`
   - `pathland-wit-host` → `pathland-view-wit`
   - `pathland-gtk-demo` → `pathland-render-gtk-demo`

5. **Preserve FFI stability (do not rename these)**
   - `[lib] name = "pathland_native"` (in `pathland-view-native`) and `name = "pathland_gtk"` (in `pathland-render-gtk`).
   - C symbols `pathland_native_*` and `pathland_gtk_*` in the `capi` modules.
   - This keeps `PathlandNative.java` / `PathlandGtk.java` (JNA), `Bridge.java`, and `run.sh`'s `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` resolution working.

6. **Update workspace + scripts**
   - `lib/rust/Cargo.toml` members list → 9 crates.
   - `generate.sh` (unchanged: `cargo run -p pathland-codegen`).
   - `lib/java/pathland-demo/run.sh`: `cargo build -p pathland-view-native -p pathland-render-gtk`.
   - Sweep every `use pathland_opcode/engine/view/host/transport` import and `Cargo.toml` path across the workspace; `codegen` uses `pathland_core::constants`.

7. **Documentation**
   - Rewrite `lib/rust/README.md` crate tree grouped by view/core/render (plus Projections / Tool / Demo); fix the engine example imports.
   - Update root `README.md` crate table and `AGENTS.md` (architecture section + run commands).

### Verification
- `cd lib/rust && cargo test` (all native crates).
- `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (guest still compiles).
- `./generate.sh` (codegen output unchanged).
- `cd lib/java/pathland-demo && ./run.sh demo.DemoHeadless` (native C ABI + GTK round-trip still works).

### Risks / notes
- The `Node`/`Component` move is the largest single change; do it in step 1 before the renames to keep `git` reviewable.
- `no_std` is preserved on `pathland-core` and `pathland-view`; `transport` stays `std` (hence its own `core`-prefixed crate rather than folding into `core`).
- Crate renames are mechanical but touch every file; `[lib] name` and FFI symbols are the only names that must not change.

Ready to execute on approval — I'd start with step 1 (the `pathland-core` consolidation) and verify tests before the rename sweep.

1: //! # pathland-view
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland SwiftUI-style view DSL. Core components (`VStack`, `HStack`,
4: //! `Text`) and chainable modifiers (`spacing`, `padding`, `font_size`, `color`,
5: //! `background`) build a retained **view tree** (`Node`) that
6: //! `pathland-engine` turns into declarative `TREE`/`STYLE` opcodes.
7: //!
8: //! ## Building a tree
9: //!
10: //! Use the `vstack!`/`hstack!` macros (which box children for you) with the
11: //! free `text`/`spacer` functions, then chain modifiers and `build()`:
12: //!
13: //! ```
14: //! use pathland_view::{vstack, hstack, text, View, ViewExt};
15: //!
16: //! let node = vstack![
17: //!     text("a"),
18: //!     hstack![text("b")],
19: //! ]
20: //! .padding(16.0)
21: //! .build();
22: //! # let _ = node;
23: //! ```
24: //!
25: //! ## Decoupled modifiers
26: //!
27: //! Modifiers are **decoupled from views** (SwiftUI-style): any modifier applies
28: //! to any view via the blanket `View::modifier`, and application code composes
29: //! **custom modifiers** from the core ones by implementing `ViewModifier`:
30: //!
31: //! ```
32: //! use pathland_view::{View, ViewExt, ViewModifier, Node, Padding, Background};
33: //!
34: //! struct Card;
35: //! impl ViewModifier for Card {
36: //!     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
37: //!         Padding(16.0).apply(node);
38: //!         Background(0xFF_EEEEEE).apply(node);
39: //!     }
40: //! }
41: //!
42: //! // Works on any view:
43: //! let a = pathland_view::text("A").modifier(Card);
44: //! let b = pathland_view::vstack![].modifier(Card);
45: //! # let _ = (a, b);
46: //! ```
47: //!
48: //! Unsupported combinations are **allowed and ignored**: the modifier emits its
49: //! property and the renderer ignores what it cannot apply.
50: //!
51: //! ## No layout math
52: //!
53: //! The DSL describes structure + constraint properties only. It never computes
54: //! bounds; native renderers lay out their own elements.
55: //!
56: //! This crate is `no_std` + `alloc`.
57: 
58: #![no_std]
59: #![forbid(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]
60: 
61: #[cfg(test)]

63: 
64: extern crate alloc;
65:

67: use alloc::rc::Rc;
68: use alloc::string::String;
69: use alloc::vec::Vec;
70: use core::cell::RefCell;

73: pub use alloc::boxed::Box;
74: /// Re-exported for `vstack!`/`hstack!` macro hygiene (`$crate::vec!`).
75: pub use alloc::vec;

77: use pathland_opcode::component_type;

86: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
87: // Core component macros + free functions
88: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
89: 
90: /// Build a vertical stack from a comma-separated list of views.
91: ///
92: /// Each child is boxed automatically, so children can mix `Text`, `HStack`,
93: /// modified views, or custom `View` implementations. Nested stacks work:
94: ///
95: /// ```
96: /// use pathland_view::{vstack, text, View};
97: /// let node = vstack![text("a"), text("b")].build();
98: /// # let _ = node;
99: /// ```
100: #[macro_export]
101: macro_rules! vstack {
102:     ($($child:expr),* $(,)?) => {
103:         $crate::VStack::new().children($crate::vec![$($crate::Box::new($child)),*])
104:     };
105: }
106: 
107: /// Build a horizontal stack from a comma-separated list of views.
108: ///
109: /// See [`vstack!`] for details.
110: #[macro_export]
111: macro_rules! hstack {
112:     ($($child:expr),* $(,)?) => {
113:         $crate::HStack::new().children($crate::vec![$($crate::Box::new($child)),*])
114:     };
115: }
116: 
117: /// A text view from a string literal (shorthand for [`Text::new`]).
118: pub fn text(content: &str) -> Text {
119:     Text::new(content)
120: }
121: 
122: /// A flexible spacer (shorthand for [`Spacer`]).
123: pub fn spacer() -> Spacer {
124:     Spacer
125: }
126: 
127: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
128: // Retained view tree
129: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
130: 
131: /// A node in the retained view tree (the application's canonical UI tree).
132: #[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
133: pub struct Node {
134:     /// Stable node id (0 until `assign_ids`).
135:     pub id: u32,
136:     pub component: Component,
137:     pub children: Vec<Node>,
138:     /// Constraint/style properties (propertyId → value) emitted as
139:     /// `STYLE:SET_PROPERTY`.
140:     pub properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,
141:     /// App-side gesture handlers (callbacks). These live only in the
142:     /// application's retained tree and are **never** emitted as protocol.
143:     pub gestures: Vec<Gesture>,
144: }
145: 
146: impl core::fmt::Debug for Node {
147:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
148:         f.debug_struct("Node")
149:             .field("id", &self.id)
150:             .field("component", &self.component)
151:             .field("children", &self.children)
152:             .field("properties", &self.properties)
153:             .field("gestures", &self.gestures.len())
154:             .finish()
155:     }
156: }
157: 
158: impl Node {
159:     /// Build an empty node (id 0, no children/properties) for a component.
160:     pub fn from_component(component: &Component) -> Self {
161:         Self {
162:             id: 0,
163:             component: component.clone(),
164:             children: Vec::new(),
165:             properties: BTreeMap::new(),
166:             gestures: Vec::new(),
167:         }
168:     }
169: }
170: 
171: /// An app-side gesture handler attached to a view.
172: ///
173: /// Callbacks live only in the application's retained tree and are **never**
174: /// emitted as protocol — the protocol carries only the declarative
175: /// `EVENT_LISTENERS` signal. Tap is the first gesture; more can be added later.
176: #[derive(Clone)]
177: pub enum Gesture {
178:     /// A tap gesture: invoke the closure when a tap is recognized.
179:     Tap(Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut() + 'static>>),
180: }
181: 
182: impl PartialEq for Gesture {
183:     fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
184:         match (self, other) {
185:             (Gesture::Tap(a), Gesture::Tap(b)) => Rc::ptr_eq(a, b),
186:         }
187:     }
188: }
189: 
190: impl core::fmt::Debug for Gesture {
191:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
192:         match self {
193:             Gesture::Tap(_) => f.write_str("Tap(..)"),
194:         }
195:     }
196: }
197: 
198: /// Core component types. These describe **structure only** — spacing, padding,
199: /// and sizing arrive as modifiers (properties), never as layout math here.
200: #[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
201: pub enum Component {
202:     /// Vertical stack (native vertical container).
203:     VStack,
204:     /// Horizontal stack (native horizontal container).
205:     HStack,
206:     /// Text leaf.
207:     Text { text: String },
208:     /// Interactive button.
209:     Button { label: String },
210:     /// Flexible spacer.
211:     Spacer,
212: }
213: 
214: impl core::fmt::Debug for Component {
215:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
216:         match self {
217:             Component::VStack => f.write_str("VStack"),
218:             Component::HStack => f.write_str("HStack"),
219:             Component::Text { text } => f.debug_tuple("Text").field(text).finish(),
220:             Component::Button { label } => f.debug_tuple("Button").field(label).finish(),
221:             Component::Spacer => f.write_str("Spacer"),
222:         }
223:     }
224: }
225: 
226: /// Map a component to its protocol component type id.
227: pub fn component_type_id(component: &Component) -> u16 {
228:     match component {
229:         Component::VStack => component_type::VSTACK,
230:         Component::HStack => component_type::HSTACK,
231:         Component::Text { .. } => component_type::TEXT,
232:         Component::Button { .. } => component_type::BUTTON,
233:         Component::Spacer => component_type::SPACER,
234:     }
235: }
236: 
237: /// Cross-axis alignment values for stacks and the `Frame` compound modifier.
238: ///
239: /// These are emitted as the `ALIGNMENT` (0x0002) property with an `ENUM` value
240: /// type (low byte of the property value).
241: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
242: pub enum Align {
243:     /// Align to the leading (start) edge.
244:     Leading,
245:     /// Center along the cross axis.
246:     Center,
247:     /// Align to the trailing (end) edge.
248:     Trailing,
249:     /// Fill the available cross-axis space.
250:     Fill,
251: }
252: 
253: impl Align {
254:     /// The protocol enum value for this alignment.
255:     pub fn value(self) -> u8 {
256:         match self {
257:             Align::Leading => 0,
258:             Align::Center => 1,
259:             Align::Trailing => 2,
260:             Align::Fill => 3,
261:         }
262:     }
263: }
264: 
265: /// The protocol value type for a property id.
266: ///
267: /// Color-valued properties (COLOR, BACKGROUND_COLOR, …) are emitted with the
268: /// `COLOR` value type; all other constraint/style properties are `F32`.
269: pub fn value_type_for(prop: u16) -> u8 {
270:     match prop {
271:         property_id::COLOR
272:         | property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR
273:         | property_id::BORDER_COLOR => pathland_opcode::value_type::COLOR,
274:         property_id::EVENT_LISTENERS => pathland_opcode::value_type::U32,
275:         _ => pathland_opcode::value_type::F32,
276:     }
277: }
278: 
279: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
280: // View protocol
281: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
282: 
283: /// A composable view. Implement for custom views; the core components and
284: /// `Modified` wrappers implement it already.
285: pub trait View {
286:     /// Build the retained node for this view.
287:     fn build(&self) -> Node;
288: }
289: 
290: /// A view decorator (SwiftUI `ViewModifier`): transforms a node's properties.
291: ///
292: /// Core modifiers (`Spacing`, `Padding`, `FontSize`, `Color`, `Background`)
293: /// implement this; application code implements it to compose custom modifiers.
294: pub trait ViewModifier {
295:     /// Apply the modifier to `node` (mutating constraint properties).
296:     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node);
297: }
298: 
299: /// A view wrapped by a modifier (SwiftUI `some View` nesting).
300: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
301: pub struct Modified<V, M> {
302:     view: V,
303:     modifier: M,
304: }
305: 
306: impl<V: View, M: ViewModifier> View for Modified<V, M> {
307:     fn build(&self) -> Node {
308:         let mut node = self.view.build();
309:         self.modifier.apply(&mut node);
310:         node
311:     }
312: }
313: 
314: /// Blanket modifier methods on any `View`.
315: ///
316: /// `.modifier(...)` applies a custom (or core) modifier; the sugar methods
317: /// (`spacing`, `padding`, `font_size`, `color`, `background`) are conveniences
318: /// that construct the corresponding core modifier. Modifiers apply
319: /// innermost-first, matching SwiftUI ordering.
320: pub trait ViewExt: View + Sized {
321:     /// Apply a modifier to this view.
322:     fn modifier<M: ViewModifier>(self, modifier: M) -> Modified<Self, M> {
323:         Modified { view: self, modifier }
324:     }
325: 
326:     /// Chain `.spacing(value)`.
327:     fn spacing(self, value: f32) -> Modified<Self, Spacing> {
328:         self.modifier(Spacing(value))
329:     }
330: 
331:     /// Chain `.padding(value)`.
332:     fn padding(self, value: f32) -> Modified<Self, Padding> {
333:         self.modifier(Padding(value))
334:     }
335: 
336:     /// Chain `.font_size(value)`.
337:     fn font_size(self, value: f32) -> Modified<Self, FontSize> {
338:         self.modifier(FontSize(value))
339:     }
340: 
341:     /// Chain `.color(rgba)` (sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`).
342:     fn color(self, rgba: u32) -> Modified<Self, Color> {
343:         self.modifier(Color(rgba))
344:     }
345: 
346:     /// Chain `.background(rgba)` (sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`).
347:     fn background(self, rgba: u32) -> Modified<Self, Background> {
348:         self.modifier(Background(rgba))
349:     }
350: 
351:     /// Chain `.frame(width, height, alignment)` — a compound sizing modifier.
352:     ///
353:     /// `width`/`height` use the `size::FILL` (-1.0) and `size::HUG_CONTENT`
354:     /// (-2.0) sentinels, or `None` to leave that axis to the native renderer.
355:     /// When an alignment is provided it is emitted as the `ALIGNMENT` property.
356:     fn frame(
357:         self,
358:         width: Option<f32>,
359:         height: Option<f32>,
360:         alignment: Option<Align>,
361:     ) -> Modified<Self, Frame> {
362:         self.modifier(Frame {
363:             width,
364:             height,
365:             alignment,
366:         })
367:     }
368: 
369:     /// Chain `.pointer_events(mask)` — declare which raw pointer events this
370:     /// view wants the renderer to report (`EVENT_LISTENERS` bitmask). This is
371:     /// what makes any element (not just a button) emit raw events; combine
372:     /// `pathland_opcode::listener::*` bits, e.g.
373:     /// `POINTER_DOWN | POINTER_UP`.
374:     fn pointer_events(self, mask: u32) -> Modified<Self, PointerEvents> {
375:         self.modifier(PointerEvents(mask))
376:     }
377: 
378:     /// Chain `.on_tap_gesture(f)` — attach a tap gesture (SwiftUI
379:     /// `onTapGesture`) to any view. The callback `f` runs when a tap is
380:     /// recognized from the view's raw pointer events (down then up on the same
381:     /// target).
382:     fn on_tap_gesture<F: FnMut() + 'static>(self, f: F) -> Modified<Self, TapGesture> {
383:         self.modifier(TapGesture(Rc::new(RefCell::new(f))))
384:     }
385: }
386: 
387: impl<T: View> ViewExt for T {}
388: 
389: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
390: // Core modifiers
391: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
392: 
393: /// Stack main-axis gap.
394: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
395: pub struct Spacing(pub f32);
396: 
397: /// Uniform padding (a styling modifier, applied to any view).
398: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
399: pub struct Padding(pub f32);
400: 
401: /// Text font size in points.
402: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
403: pub struct FontSize(pub f32);
404: 
405: /// Text/foreground color (sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`).
406: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
407: pub struct Color(pub u32);
408: 
409: /// Background color (sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`).
410: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
411: pub struct Background(pub u32);
412: 
413: /// The compound `frame` sizing modifier (SwiftUI `frame`).
414: ///
415: /// Emits `WIDTH`, `HEIGHT`, and optionally `ALIGNMENT` as ordinary
416: /// `SET_PROPERTY` values. `width`/`height` use the `size::FILL` (-1.0) and
417: /// `size::HUG_CONTENT` (-2.0) sentinels; `None` leaves that axis to the native
418: /// renderer.
419: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
420: pub struct Frame {
421:     pub width: Option<f32>,
422:     pub height: Option<f32>,
423:     pub alignment: Option<Align>,
424: }
425: 
426: /// Declares which raw pointer events a view wants reported (the `EVENT_LISTENERS`
427: /// u32 bitmask, e.g. `listener::POINTER_DOWN | listener::POINTER_UP`). Applies to
428: /// any view; the renderer attaches native input recognition for the requested
429: /// events.
430: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
431: pub struct PointerEvents(pub u32);
432: 
433: /// A tap-gesture modifier (SwiftUI `onTapGesture`). Declares the pointer
434: /// down/up listeners and stores the app-side callback in the node's gesture
435: /// list.
436: #[derive(Clone)]
437: pub struct TapGesture(Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut() + 'static>>);
438: 
439: impl PartialEq for TapGesture {
440:     fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
441:         Rc::ptr_eq(&self.0, &other.0)
442:     }
443: }
444: 
445: impl core::fmt::Debug for TapGesture {
446:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
447:         f.write_str("TapGesture(..)")
448:     }
449: }

451: impl ViewModifier for Spacing {
452:     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
453:         node.properties.insert(property_id::SPACING, self.0.to_bits());
454:     }
455: }
456: 
457: impl ViewModifier for Padding {
458:     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
459:         node.properties.insert(property_id::PADDING, self.0.to_bits());
460:     }
461: }
462: 
463: impl ViewModifier for FontSize {
464:     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
465:         node.properties
466:             .insert(property_id::FONT_SIZE, self.0.to_bits());
467:     }
468: }
469: 
470: impl ViewModifier for Color {

473:     }
474: }
475: 
476: impl ViewModifier for Background {

479:     }
480: }
